answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. The protocol caps each account’s influence and slashes the stake when independently checked work is fraudulent, so creating many accounts does not create free voting power: every Sybil must tie up capital and risk losing it. For example, cedar, shale, and onyx can each name an agent, but none gains extra weight without another costly stake. This raises the attacker’s funding cost while honest agents retain recoverable deposits.
